clinician.trajectory_summary: A 31-year-old woman with known Child's B liver cirrhosis and portal hypertension presented with one month of dull left hypochondriac abdominal pain and physical exam showing Hackett's Grade 2 splenomegaly. Initial blood counts showed low WBC (1.9 x 10^9/L) and platelets (54 x 10^9/L). Follow-up labs indicated improvement in blood counts (WBC 5.0 x 10^9/L, platelets 209 x 10^9/L). Imaging via follow-up abdominal CT showed reduction in spleen size, supporting hypersplenism as part of the clinical picture. While bone marrow biopsy results were not documented, the clinical course including cytopenias and splenomegaly alongside improvement and imaging findings supports the diagnosis of severe aplastic anemia (SAA) coexisting with hypersplenism secondary to portal hypertension. The initial left hypochondriac pain correlates with splenic enlargement.
